title: Sum an Array
description: Given an array of numbers, return the sum of all elements. If the array is empty, return 0.
whatShouldHappen: Start with a running total of 0.
Visit every element in the array from left to right.
Add each element to the running total.
Return the total after the loop ends.
patternExplanation: The accumulator pattern initializes a variable before the loop and updates it on every iteration, producing a single result from a collection.

title: Find the Max
description: Given a non-empty array of numbers, return the largest value. Do not use Math.max.
whatShouldHappen: Assume the first element is the current maximum.
If an element is larger than the current maximum, update the maximum.
Return the maximum after the loop.
patternExplanation: Seed a variable with the first element, then scan the rest — update whenever a larger value is found. Works in a single pass without sorting.

title: Count Even Numbers
description: Given an array of integers, return how many of them are even.
whatShouldHappen: Loop through every element in the array.
If the element is divisible by 2 (num % 2 === 0), increment the counter.
Return the counter after the loop.
patternExplanation: A conditional counter increments only when a condition is met — combining a loop with an if-statement to tally matching elements.

title: FizzBuzz
description: Given a number n, return an array of strings from 1 to n. For multiples of 3 use "Fizz", multiples of 5 use "Buzz", multiples of both use "FizzBuzz", otherwise use the number as a string.
whatShouldHappen: Check divisibility by 15 first (both 3 and 5) — push "FizzBuzz".
Otherwise push the number converted to a string.
patternExplanation: Order your conditions from most specific (divisible by 15) to least specific — otherwise the 3 or 5 check will match before the combined case.

title: Find First Duplicate
description: Given an array of integers, return the first element that appears more than once. If no duplicate exists, return -1. The "first" duplicate is the one whose second occurrence appears earliest in the array.
whatShouldHappen: Use a Set to track elements you have already seen.
Loop through the array from left to right.
For each element, check if it is already in the Set.
If yes, return it immediately — it is the first duplicate.
Otherwise add it to the Set and continue.
Return -1 if the loop finishes without finding a duplicate.
patternExplanation: A Set tracks membership in O(1) time. Checking seen.has() before seen.add() on each element catches the first repeated value in a single linear pass.

title: Count Occurrences of a Target
description: Given an array of numbers and a target value, count how many times the target appears in the array.
whatShouldHappen: Iterate through nums from index 0 to nums.length - 1.
Return count after the loop completes.
patternExplanation: A standard linear scan with an accumulator counter tracks match occurrences in O(n) time.

title: Find Minimum and Maximum
description: Given a non-empty array of numbers, return an array [min, max] containing the smallest and largest numbers found.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize min = nums[0] and max = nums[0].
If nums[i] < min, update min = nums[i].
If nums[i] > max, update max = nums[i].
patternExplanation: Initializing extremes with the first item and updating in a single pass finds min and max in O(n) without sorting.

title: Calculate Average
description: Given an array of numbers, return the mathematical average (mean) of all values. If the array is empty, return 0.
whatShouldHappen: Loop over nums adding each value to sum.
patternExplanation: Accumulate total sum in O(n) and divide by length, guarding against division by zero on empty input.

title: Sum Digits with While Loop
description: Given a non-negative integer num, return the sum of its individual digits. Use a while loop with modulo (%) and division (Math.floor) to extract digits from right to left.
whatShouldHappen: Handle edge case: if num is 0, return 0.
While num > 0, extract the last digit with num % 10 and add it to sum.
Remove the last digit by updating num = Math.floor(num / 10).
patternExplanation: Using while (n > 0) paired with n % 10 and Math.floor(n / 10) is the standard pattern for extracting and processing integer digits without converting to strings.

title: Count Collatz Steps
description: Given a positive integer n, return the number of steps required to reach 1 following the Collatz sequence: if n is even, divide it by 2 (n / 2); if n is odd, multiply by 3 and add 1 (3 * n + 1). If n is already 1, return 0.
whatShouldHappen: While n is not equal to 1, check if n is even or odd using n % 2 === 0.
If even, divide n by 2; if odd, update n to 3 * n + 1.
Return total steps when n becomes 1.
patternExplanation: While loops with condition-dependent updates model state-transition algorithms where the number of iterations cannot be known upfront.

title: Count Halvings with Do-While
description: Given a positive integer n, use a do...while loop to repeatedly divide n by 2 (using Math.floor(n / 2)) until n is 1 or less. Return the total count of halvings performed. Because do...while always executes at least once, n = 1 will be halved once (resulting in 0) and return 1.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize count to 0 and current to n.
Execute do block: update current = Math.floor(current / 2) and increment count.
patternExplanation: A do...while loop guarantees the loop body runs at least once before testing its exit condition, making it ideal for processes requiring at least one initial reduction.

title: Compute Integer Power with While Loop
description: Given non-negative integers base and exp, compute base raised to the power exp using a while loop and compound multiplication (*=). Do not use Math.pow or the ** operator.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize result to 1 (since any number to power 0 is 1).
While remainingExp > 0, multiply result by base and decrement remainingExp by 1.
patternExplanation: Starting an accumulator at 1 and multiplying by a factor across iterations is the foundation of powers, factorials, and compound scaling.

title: Sum Until Sentinel with Break
description: Given an array of numbers nums and a sentinel value stopVal, iterate from left to right and sum all numbers until encountering stopVal. Once stopVal is encountered, immediately terminate the loop using the break keyword without adding stopVal to the total.
whatShouldHappen: Iterate through nums from index 0 to nums.length - 1.
If the current number strictly equals stopVal, break out of the loop.
Otherwise, add current number to total.
patternExplanation: The break statement allows early termination of loops as soon as a stop condition or sentinel value is detected, preventing unnecessary iterations.

title: Math.floor: Integer Division
description: Given numbers a and b (b !== 0), return the integer floor quotient using Math.floor(a / b).
patternExplanation: Math.floor() rounds a floating-point number downward to the nearest integer.

title: Math.ceil: Calculate Pagination Total Pages
description: Given totalItems count and items perPage (perPage > 0), return total pages needed using Math.ceil(totalItems / perPage). If totalItems is 0, return 0.
patternExplanation: Math.ceil() rounds upwards, guaranteeing any fractional remaining items receive a dedicated page.

tests.label: 25 items with 10 per page requires 3 pages

title: Math.round: Round to Two Decimals
description: Given floating-point number num, round it to 2 decimal places using Math.round(num * 100) / 100.
patternExplanation: Multiplying by 10^k, applying Math.round, and dividing back by 10^k rounds to k decimal places.

title: Math.trunc: Truncate Fractional Part
description: Given number num, use Math.trunc(num) to return the integer part by removing all fractional digits without rounding.
patternExplanation: Math.trunc() discards fractional digits, truncating towards zero unlike Math.floor().

title: Math.round: Round to Nearest Multiple of Five
description: Given integer num, round it to the nearest multiple of 5 using Math.round(num / 5) * 5.
patternExplanation: Dividing by step size, rounding, and multiplying by step snaps values to numeric intervals.

title: Math.abs: Absolute Difference
description: Given numbers a and b, return their non-negative distance using Math.abs(a - b).
patternExplanation: Math.abs() returns the positive magnitude of a number, computing distance regardless of order.

title: Math.sign: Determine Number Sign
description: Given number n, use Math.sign(n) to return 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if 0, or -0 if -0.
patternExplanation: Math.sign() evaluates the sign of a number directly without conditional branching.

title: Math.min & Math.max: Clamp Number in Range
description: Given val, lower bound min, and upper bound max (min <= max), return val clamped so it never drops below min or exceeds max using Math.min and Math.max.
patternExplanation: Nesting Math.max and Math.min restricts inputs to boundaries [min, max].

title: Math.hypot: Euclidean Distance from Origin
description: Given 2D coordinates x and y, use Math.hypot(x, y) to return the distance from the origin (0, 0) without intermediate squaring overflow.
patternExplanation: Math.hypot() computes sqrt(x^2 + y^2) avoiding intermediate magnitude overflow.

title: Math.abs: Manhattan Grid Distance
description: Given two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), return their Manhattan (taxicab) distance: Math.abs(x1 - x2) + Math.abs(y1 - y2).
patternExplanation: Summing absolute orthogonal coordinate differences measures grid-based distance.

title: Math.sqrt: Verify Perfect Square
description: Given non-negative integer n, return true if n is a perfect square (i.e. Math.floor(Math.sqrt(n)) ** 2 === n).
patternExplanation: Comparing the floored square root squared against the input checks integer squareness.

title: Math.cbrt: Cube Root Extraction
description: Given number n, use Math.round(Math.cbrt(n)) to return the rounded cube root.
patternExplanation: Math.cbrt() accurately computes cube roots, properly preserving negative signs.

title: Math.pow: Compute Base to Power
description: Given base and exponent exp, return Math.pow(base, exp).
patternExplanation: Math.pow(base, exponent) raises numbers to positive or fractional powers.

title: Math.log2: Check Power of Two
description: Given positive integer n, return true if Math.log2(n) is an integer (i.e. Number.isInteger(Math.log2(n))), otherwise false.
patternExplanation: Math.log2() computes base-2 logarithms, returning integers for exact powers of two.

title: Math.hypot: Validate Right Triangle Sides
description: Given legs a, b, and hypotenuse c, return true if Math.hypot(a, b) === c.
patternExplanation: Math.hypot() directly evaluates the Pythagorean theorem a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

title: Math.min & Math.max: Spread Array Bounds
description: Given a non-empty array nums, return an object { min: Math.min(...nums), max: Math.max(...nums) }.
patternExplanation: Spreading array arguments into Math.min and Math.max retrieves bounding values in one expression.

title: Math: Array Dynamic Range Span
description: Given an array nums of at least 2 numbers, return the difference between the maximum and minimum values using Math.max and Math.min.
patternExplanation: Subtracting Math.min from Math.max measures the dynamic dispersion span of an array.

title: Math.max: Find Second Largest Number
description: Given an array nums with at least 2 distinct numbers, return the second largest value.
whatShouldHappen: Filter out elements strictly equal to max.
patternExplanation: Filtering out the global maximum and taking the maximum of remaining elements finds the second largest value.

title: Math.min & max: Clamp All Array Values
description: Given an array nums, minBound, and maxBound, return a new array where every element is clamped within [minBound, maxBound].
whatShouldHappen: Map nums: n => Math.min(Math.max(n, minBound), maxBound).
patternExplanation: Mapping vector coordinates through clamp boundaries confines signals within operating limits.

title: Math.abs: Find Number Closest to Target
description: Given array nums and target, return the number in nums that minimizes Math.abs(n - target). If tied, return the first one encountered.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize closest = nums[0], minDiff = Math.abs(nums[0] - target).
Loop n of nums: diff = Math.abs(n - target).
If diff < minDiff: update minDiff = diff, closest = n.
patternExplanation: Tracking minimum absolute deviation identifies the closest scalar value.

title: Number.parseInt: Binary String to Decimal
description: Given binary string binStr (e.g. "1011"), use Number.parseInt(binStr, 2) to convert it to a decimal integer.
patternExplanation: Number.parseInt(str, radix) specifies base-2 decoding for binary strings.

title: Number.parseInt: Hexadecimal String to Decimal
description: Given hexadecimal string hexStr (e.g. "ff" or "1A"), use Number.parseInt(hexStr, 16) to convert it to decimal.
patternExplanation: Number.parseInt with radix 16 parses base-16 hexadecimal representations.

title: Number.prototype.toString: Decimal to Binary
description: Given non-negative integer num, convert it to a binary string representation using num.toString(2).
patternExplanation: num.toString(radix) converts integer numbers into string representations in base 2 through 36.

title: Number.parseFloat: Parse Currency Price
description: Given a price string like "$19.99" or "49.50 USD", strip non-numeric prefix characters and parse it into a floating-point number using Number.parseFloat.
whatShouldHappen: Remove non-digits and non-dots from start using priceStr.replace(/^[^0-9.]+/, '').
patternExplanation: Number.parseFloat parses decimal numbers up to the first invalid non-numeric character.

title: Number.prototype.toString: Decimal to Hexadecimal
description: Given a non-negative integer num, return its lowercase hexadecimal string representation using num.toString(16).
patternExplanation: num.toString(16) produces lowercase hexadecimal representations (0-9, a-f).

title: Number.isInteger: Filter Integer Elements
description: Given an array mixedList containing numbers and floats, use mixedList.filter(Number.isInteger) to return only the whole integers.
patternExplanation: Number.isInteger() verifies that a value is of type number and has zero fractional component.

title: Number.isNaN: Filter Valid Parsed Numbers
description: Given an array of strings strArr, convert each item to a number using Number(s), and return an array containing only the valid numbers using .filter(n => !Number.isNaN(n)).
whatShouldHappen: Map strings to numbers: strArr.map(s => Number(s)).
patternExplanation: Number.isNaN() strictly verifies NaN without the faulty coercion of the global isNaN function.

title: Number.isFinite: Verify Safe Division
description: Given a numerator and denominator, divide numerator by denominator and return whether the result is a finite number using Number.isFinite(numerator / denominator).
patternExplanation: Number.isFinite() rejects Infinity, -Infinity, and NaN without coercing non-numbers.

tests.label: zero divided by zero yields NaN

title: Number.isSafeInteger: Precision Boundary Check
description: Given number num, use Number.isSafeInteger(num) to check if it falls within the IEEE-754 double precision exact integer range [-(2^53 - 1), 2^53 - 1].
patternExplanation: Number.isSafeInteger() guards against 64-bit floating-point precision truncation for large integers.

title: Arithmetic Operator: Safe Division Guard
description: Given numbers a and b, return a / b if b !== 0. If b === 0, return null to prevent Infinity/division by zero.
patternExplanation: Guarding divisor b === 0 prevents unhandled Infinity or NaN propagation in calculations.

title: Greatest Common Divisor (Euclidean)
description: Calculate the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two non-zero positive integers `a` and `b` using the Euclidean algorithm and a while loop with the remainder operator `%`.
whatShouldHappen: While remainder b is not 0, store b in a temp variable
patternExplanation: The Euclidean algorithm repeatedly computes remainders until b is 0, leaving the GCD in a.

title: Convert Decimal to Binary with Loop
description: Convert a non-negative integer `n` into its binary string representation using a while loop with `% 2` and `Math.floor(n / 2)`. For 0, return `"0"`.
whatShouldHappen: Loop while num > 0: prepend (num % 2) to binary string
patternExplanation: Repeatedly extracting the least significant bit with % 2 and shifting right by dividing by 2 generates the binary representation.

title: Count Prime Factors
description: Count the total number of prime factors (with multiplicity) of an integer `n` (`n >= 2`) using nested while/for loops and `%`.
whatShouldHappen: While d * d <= num: while num % d === 0, increment count and num = Math.floor(num / d)
If num > 1, increment count for the remaining prime factor
patternExplanation: Factoring out each divisor as long as it divides evenly factors the number in O(sqrt(n)) time.

title: Reverse Integer Digits
description: Reverse the digits of a non-negative integer `n` purely mathematically using a while loop, `% 10`, and `Math.floor(n / 10)`. Do not convert to string.
patternExplanation: Peeling off the last digit with % 10 and pushing it into rev by multiplying by 10 reverses any integer mathematically.

title: Numeric Palindrome Check
description: Check whether a non-negative integer `n` is a palindrome (reads the same backwards as forwards) using arithmetic loop operations.
whatShouldHappen: Compute the reversed number using a while loop and arithmetic
patternExplanation: Comparing the mathematically reversed number to the original number tests for palindromic symmetry.

title: Two Pointers with Comma Operator
description: Reverse an array into a new array by using two pointers `i` and `j` in a single for loop header utilizing the JavaScript comma operator (`for (let i = 0, j = arr.length - 1; i < arr.length; i++, j--)`).
whatShouldHappen: Create a new array of length arr.length
Use a for loop header with two variables i and j separated by comma: for (let i = 0, j = arr.length - 1; i < arr.length; i++, j--)
patternExplanation: The comma operator in the loop initialization and update clause allows managing multiple index variables simultaneously.

title: Word Frequency with Logical OR Assignment
description: Build a word frequency counter object from an array of words using a for...of loop and the logical OR assignment operator `counts[word] ||= 0; counts[word]++;`.
whatShouldHappen: Use counts[word] ||= 0 to set to 0 if falsy, then increment
patternExplanation: Logical OR assignment (a ||= b) assigns b to a only if a is falsy, initializing missing keys cleanly.

title: Strict Validity Pass with Logical AND Assignment
description: Given an array of numeric test scores, iterate through them with a for...of loop and update a boolean status `let valid = true;` using the logical AND assignment operator `valid &&= (score >= minThreshold);`. Return the final boolean.
patternExplanation: Logical AND assignment (a &&= b) only evaluates and keeps truthy if both operands are truthy, acting as an accumulator guard.

title: Default Config Merge with Nullish Assignment
description: Given an options object and an array of default [key, defaultValue] pairs, iterate through the defaults and apply them to options using the nullish coalescing assignment operator `opts[key] ??= defaultValue`. Return the modified options object.
whatShouldHappen: Create a shallow copy of options: const res = { ...options }
Iterate through defaults pairs with for...of
patternExplanation: Nullish coalescing assignment (a ??= b) only assigns when a is null or undefined, preserving falsy values like 0, false, and empty string.

title: Find Target in 2D Matrix with Labeled Break
description: Given a 2D matrix (array of arrays) and a target value, find the [row, col] coordinates of its first occurrence using nested for loops with a labeled break statement (`search: for (...)`). If not found, return [-1, -1].
whatShouldHappen: Label outer loop: outer: for (let r = 0; r < matrix.length; r++)
Inner loop through columns: if matrix[r][c] === target, set result = [r, c] and break outer
patternExplanation: A labeled break statement terminates the outer loop immediately without needing additional boolean flag variables.
